title: Nature Therapy and Hypnotherapy for Patients with Mild to Moderate Depression – A Randomized, Three-Arm, Single-Center, Confirmatory, Controlled Study Using a Mixed-Methods Approach
summary:
The lifetime risk of developing depression is approximately 16–20% both nationally and internationally. Women are statistically more likely to be affected than men. Depressive disorders are characterized by low mood, loss of interest, reduced energy, and a variety of physical and cognitive symptoms.
The aim of the confirmatory, eight-week intervention study “NatureDeep” is to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and feasibility of nature-based therapy and hypnotherapy compared to routine care alone (“treatment as usual”) in adult patients with mild to 
moderate depression.
The study comprises three groups:
1. Nature-based therapy + routine care
2. Hypnotherapy + routine care
3. Routine care alone (control group)
All study interventions span a period of eight weeks and take place once a week 
in groups of up to ten participants. The hypnotherapy sessions are conducted in group settings indoor settings, while nature-based therapy takes place in person in a natural environment (urban forest). 
All participants may continue their existing psychotherapeutic treatment and (if already 
prescribed) continue taking antidepressants. The study is scheduled to begin in April 2026. Participation will take place in Berlin.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
A specialist diagnosis of mild to moderate depression according to the DSM-5 criteria
The patient’s willingness to be randomized and to participate in the interventions and examinations as part of the study, as well as to complete questionnaires and diaries
Proficiency in the German language
Intact hearing and speech comprehension
Sufficient mobility to participate in nature therapy
The patient is capable of giving informed consent and is cognitively and linguistically able to assess the significance of the study
Signed informed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
1)    Severe mental health conditions: major depressive disorder, past or current psychosis, acute self-harm or suicidal tendencies, post-traumatic stress disorder, personality disorder, substance use disorder, severe anxiety disorder
2)	Moderate or severe acute or chronic physical illness, such as cancer or severe autoimmune diseases, that could affect study participation.
3)    Current treatment or treatment within the last 3 months with naturopathy and/or hypnosis
4)    Planned initiation of antidepressant medication within the next 16 weeks or recent initiation of antidepressant medication within the last 3 months
5)	Planned start of psychotherapy within the next 16 weeks or start of psychotherapy within 3 months prior to study enrollment
6)    Planned participation in an intervention study during the same period as the study or within the last 3 months prior to the start of the study
7)    Affiliation with the study center (e.g., employee)
8)	Current application for disability benefits
9)    Application for rehabilitation under review
10)    Not used regularly (at least 3 times a week) and should not be newly introduced: mind-body medicine, autogenic training, hypnosis, natural therapies
11)    Pregnancy and breastfeeding
